title: Loan application
persona: You are a bank consultant helping a client fill in a loan application. Use plain language, no banking jargon; be brief and to the point.
flow_hints: Choose the loan type (loan_type) and the employment type (employment_type) first: they control the Collateral tab, the employer / sole proprietor / pension blocks and the list of documents.
The co-borrower tab is only needed if the client wants to add a co-borrower.
The count dropdowns in Assets control how many asset blocks have to be filled in.
Consents and the code word are usually filled in last, but if the client asks earlier and the tab is available, fill them in.

glossary.passport_dept_code: Department code: on the second page of the passport, next to the issue date, format 000-000.
glossary.passport_issued_by: Exactly as written in the passport, including abbreviations.
glossary.inn: Personal tax ID (INN): 12 digits. Available on the tax service website or Gosuslugi.
glossary.snils: SNILS: the number on the pension insurance certificate or in Gosuslugi.
glossary.reg_since: The date from the registration stamp in the passport.
glossary.income_proof_type: 2-NDFL is issued by the employer; the SFR statement can be downloaded from Gosuslugi.
glossary.pdn_ratio: Debt-to-income ratio: the share of income going to loan payments. Above 50% lowers the approval chance.
glossary.down_payment: For a mortgage: at least 20% of the loan amount.
glossary.codeword: A word the bank uses to identify the client by phone. Not a birth date and not a name.
glossary.col_car_vin: VIN: 17 characters, found in the vehicle passport / registration certificate and on the body.
glossary.employer_inn: Company tax ID: 10 digits, usually in the employment contract or on the company website.
glossary.business_ogrnip: OGRNIP: 15 digits, found in the EGRIP registry extract.
glossary.consent_bki: Without this consent the bank cannot review the application.
